newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo to launch several cars before 2000.
newsitem.headline: Volvo to launch several cars before 2000.

text.p: Swedish automotive group Volvo said on Thursday its Cars division would launch several new models before the end of the decade.
"The new models will help Volvo reach its target of selling 500,000 cars per year by the end of the century," Volvo spokesman Ingemar Hesslefors told Reuters.
Volvo will be using two industrial platforms as the basis of its car production. The basis of the first platform will be the new S40/V40 series.

"We'll be making several models from the same platform," Hesslefors said, adding that even though the models would have many similarities, the customer would experience them as totally different cars.
The large platform could be based around the successor to the current 850 series, he said.
"It's possible that we'll do that. It will in any case be a platform for larger passenger cars. You will have seen that platform by the end of the decade," Hesselfors said.

He said Volvo Cars had invested 4.5 billion crowns in research and development costs over the past year, mainly in the development of the S40/V40, he said, adding that the figure would remain high over the years to come.
Hesslefors said the S40/V40 range would begin to make its mark in sales figures during the third quarter of this year.
